about: Every number and named source this video shows or says, with its source. Trade sources only (Todd, Oct 28, 2026: evidence from the trades). Each page opened and re-read on Oct 28, 2026 (Central); the note is the page's own sentence. Checked by the facts gate against the source pages.

firstVisit.title: Follow-Ups 101: Back 2 Basics
firstVisit.publisher: ServiceTitan (blog, webinar recap by Mike LaFollette)
firstVisit.kind: vendor data, method not shown; said on screen and in voice as ServiceTitan's own data
firstVisit.note: Page description: "Only 37% of estimates close on the first visit." Body: "ServiceTitan data shows only 37% convert immediately, which leaves the majority of opportunities dependent on follow-up."
firstVisit.textVsEmail: qualitative, no number: "Burgess notes how text messages consistently outperform email, with significantly higher open rates." Brittany Burgess, Sr. Customer Advocacy Specialist at ServiceTitan, one of the webinar's two presenters. Said as "ServiceTitan's follow-up webinar says texts beat email on open rates."
firstVisit.doNotUse: the same page's 64%, 72% and 87% figures and its "at least four times" advice that rests on them (KNOWLEDGE.md do-not-use list)

homeowners.title: The new home service standard: Why systems now win more customers
homeowners.population: U.S. homeowners, online via SurveyMonkey Audience, fielded October 23, 2025
homeowners.kind: vendor survey (home service software maker); said as "a Housecall Pro survey"
homeowners.note: Chart: "59% expect text updates". Body: "many now anticipate text updates as the job progresses." Method: "This survey was conducted online on October 23, 2025, with 1,040 U.S. homeowners via SurveyMonkey Audience." Scope: text updates on a job, not quote follow-ups; the script says "expect text updates" and nothing more.

cadence.title: Quote Follow-Up Email Templates: 7 Examples to Close More Jobs
cadence.daysNote: 24 to 48 hours, said as "a day or two"
cadence.kind: practice advice for quote follow-ups (written for email), not data; said as "Jobber says" and on screen as Jobber's timing
cadence.note: First follow-up "should land in their inbox within two days after sending the quote"; "you can send your next email one week after sending your initial quote"; "it's best to send your final follow-up 24-48 hours before the quote expires"; "If you haven't heard back after your third follow-up, it's OK to close the file and move on."
cadence.personalNote: Checklist: "personalized elements, like the client name and project details". Sample: "Do you have any questions about the quote we sent on [date]?"; FAQ: "Asking if the customer has any questions" so a follow-up doesn't sound pushy. Said as "Use their name, name the job, and ask a question."
